mixing_rules.lichtenecker: ln eps = phi1 ln eps1 + phi2 ln eps2

assumptions: volume fractions come from pure-component molar volumes at the matched temperature, i.e. zero excess volume of mixing
the pure-component epsilon is the nearest value within 5 K anywhere in the corpus; the same-DOI flag records when it came from the mixture's own study
only 2-component datasets with a molar composition variable are used

association_classification.rule: a pair is PROTIC_PRESENT if either pure component has HBD>0 in its molecular descriptor row; UNKNOWN if either component has no resolved structure
association_classification.source: CORE239 descriptor table + newly resolved PubChem structures; no name-based chemical guessing

clausius_mossotti_domain.why: the CM rule maps eps to f=(eps-1)/(eps+2) in [0,1) and inverts g=(eps-1)/(eps+2); when the volume-fraction-weighted g reaches 0.49 the predicted eps diverges, so the rule is formally undefined for water-rich and other high-permittivity mixtures
clausius_mossotti_domain.consequence: the CM comparison is restricted to the low-epsilon part of the composition space; it must NOT be quoted as covering the whole dataset, and the protic class is under-represented there. Lichtenecker is the rule defined on every point.

sign_of_the_residual: measured epsilon exceeds every ideal rule on median in BOTH association classes; the protic residual is the larger one, i.e. the departure grows with H-bond capability rather than with polarity alone

same_doi_pure_reference.note: most reference epsilon values come from a different study than the mixture; this is a cross-source splice of the REFERENCE, which is recorded per row and must not be hidden

what_this_can_and_cannot_say: CAN: quantify how far measured mixture epsilon departs from three fixed ideal mixing rules, and whether the departure is systematically larger for H-bonding pairs
CANNOT: turn that residual into an association parameter or a Kirkwood g; the rules are not derived from a molecular model of the mixture
CANNOT: be used as a training label set -- no mixture record enters the single-molecule epsilon model
